extensionDescription.message: Run filter rules on any folder on a schedule, not just the Inbox. Match by sender, subject, address book, or SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
extensionDescription.description: Short description shown in the add-ons manager.

common_addSpamDomains.description: Right-click menu item and title of the window that adds the sender domains of the selected messages to a spam rule.

common_runAllRulesNow.description: Button on the settings page and in the toolbar popup, and a right-click menu item. Runs every rule once, right away.

common_restoreDefaults.description: Button that puts the settings of a section back to their default values.

common_allowTagAccess.description: Button that asks Thunderbird for permission to list the user's message tags.

common_noTag.description: Shown in place of a tag name when no tag is chosen.

common_untitledRule.description: Name used for a rule whose name is empty.

common_quoted.description: A rule name in quotation marks, inside a longer message. Use the quotation marks of your language. $1 is the name.

menu_runARule.description: Right-click submenu that lists the rules; choosing one runs it.

options_theme.description: Label for the light, dark, and system theme switch. Read by screen readers only.

options_themeSystem.description: Theme switch: follow the Thunderbird theme. Read by screen readers only.

options_themeSystemTitle.description: Tooltip of the theme switch button that follows the Thunderbird theme.

options_tagline.message: Run rules on any folder on a timer — the piece stock Thunderbird only does for the Inbox.
options_tagline.description: One-line explanation under the page title.

options_runEvery.description: Label around the number box for the default timer. $1 is the number box; keep it.

options_save.description: Button that saves every rule and setting on the page.

options_collapseAll.description: Button that folds every rule card to a one-line summary.

options_expandAll.description: Button that opens every folded rule card.

options_export.description: Button that saves the rules to a JSON file.

options_import.description: Button that loads rules from a JSON file.

options_addRule.description: Button that adds an empty rule card.

allowlist_title.description: Heading of the section with the domains that Add spam domains never adds.

allowlist_hint.message: Domains here are skipped when adding spam domains from the message list, so a mistaken selection cannot block a major provider. One domain per line.
allowlist_hint.description: Explanation of the protected domains list.

diag_title.description: Heading of the section with the diagnostics report.

diag_hint.message: If something does not behave as expected, send this report along with your message. It lists your Thunderbird version, the shape of each rule, and what recent runs did. Addresses, domains, patterns and folder names are left out unless you tick the box below. What you see here is exactly what will be shared.
diag_hint.description: Explanation of the diagnostics report. The report itself stays in English.

diag_includeValues.message: Include rule values (addresses, domains, patterns, folders)
diag_includeValues.description: Checkbox that adds the values of each rule to the diagnostics report.

diag_copy.description: Button that copies the diagnostics report to the clipboard.

diag_save.description: Button that saves the diagnostics report to a text file.

diag_refresh.description: Button that rebuilds the diagnostics report.

diag_clear.description: Button that deletes the diagnostics log.

diag_buildFailed.description: Shown in the report box when the report fails. $1 is the error message, in English.

adv_title.description: Heading of the Advanced settings section. Other messages refer to it in …; use the same word there.

adv_hint.message: Timings for the scan engine. The defaults suit most people; change them only if you know why. Every value is clamped to a safe range when you save.
adv_hint.description: Explanation at the top of the Advanced section.

adv_logScheduleRuns.message: Log every run on a rule's own schedule

adv_logScheduleRunsHint.message: Without this, the diagnostics log records such a run only when it changes mail or fails. A rule that runs every minute would otherwise push the older entries out of the log within hours. Select Save to apply a change.
adv_logScheduleRunsHint.description: Explanation of the checkbox that logs every scheduled run. Keep … around the name of the Save button.

adv_runOnNewMail.message: Also run when new mail arrives

adv_runOnNewMailHint.message: Without this, rules only run on the timer above, so new mail waits up to that long. Thunderbird reports each arrival as it happens.
adv_runOnNewMailHint.description: Explanation of the checkbox that runs rules on new mail.

adv_newMailDelay.message: Wait $1 seconds after the last arrival before running
adv_newMailDelay.description: Label around a number box. $1 is the number box; keep it.

adv_newMailDelayHint.message: One mail sync reports many messages. Waiting collapses the whole batch into a single run. Capped at 15 seconds because Thunderbird suspends idle add-ons.
adv_newMailDelayHint.description: Explanation of the delay before a run on new mail.

adv_catchUp.message: Catch-up scan every $1 minutes, covering the last $2 days
adv_catchUp.description: Label around two number boxes. $1 is the box for the minutes and $2 the box for the days; keep both.

adv_catchUpHint.message: Normal runs only look at mail dated since the previous run. A sender can backdate the Date header, so this wider pass catches mail those runs missed. Raising either number costs more work per pass.
adv_catchUpHint.description: Explanation of the catch-up scan. Date is the name of a mail header; keep it.

adv_overlap.message: Overlap each normal scan by $1 minutes
adv_overlap.description: Label around a number box. $1 is the number box; keep it.

adv_overlapHint.message: How far before the previous run each scan starts, so mail arriving mid-scan or dated slightly early is not missed.

adv_showMenu.message: Show Folder Filter Scheduler in the right-click menu
adv_showMenu.description: Checkbox in the Advanced section. Folder Filter Scheduler is the name of the extension.

adv_showMenuHint.message: The menu adds spam domains and runs rules from the message list. Without it, the toolbar button and this page still run rules. Select Save to apply a change.
adv_showMenuHint.description: Explanation of the right-click menu checkbox. Keep … around the name of the Save button.

adv_shortName.message: Use the short name FFS on the toolbar button and in the right-click menu
adv_shortName.description: Checkbox in the Advanced section. FFS is the short name of the extension; keep it.

adv_shortNameHint.message: The short name takes less room. The tooltip of the toolbar button keeps the full name. Select Save to apply a change.
adv_shortNameHint.description: Explanation of the short name checkbox. Keep … around the name of the Save button.

adv_authHeading.description: Subheading in the Advanced section for the SPF, DKIM, and DMARC settings.

adv_authOwn.description: Checkbox: the add-on checks DKIM signatures itself instead of trusting the mail provider. DKIM is a technical name; keep it.

adv_authOwnHint.message: A sender can add a fake Authentication-Results header, so the add-on verifies DKIM signatures itself and works out DMARC from the result. It downloads each full message an authentication condition looks at and asks the DNS server below for the signing key. The server sees the domain names it is asked about. Without this, the add-on reads DKIM and DMARC from the header your mail provider adds.
adv_authOwnHint.description: Explanation of the own DKIM check. Keep Authentication-Results as is: it is the name of a mail header.

adv_authServer.description: Label in front of the list of DNS servers. $1 is the list; keep it.

adv_authServerHint.message: Thunderbird asks you to allow the server the first time you use it.
adv_authServerHint.description: Explanation under the DNS server list.

adv_authPrefer.message: When my check and the provider's header disagree, use $1
adv_authPrefer.description: Label around a list with two choices: adv_authPreferOwn and adv_authPreferProvider. $1 is the list; keep it.

adv_authPreferOwn.description: Choice in the list after "When my check and the provider's header disagree, use".

adv_authPreferProvider.description: Choice in the list after "When my check and the provider's header disagree, use".

adv_authPreferHint.message: With the provider's header, the add-on uses its own result only for a check that the header doesn't report.
adv_authPreferHint.description: Explanation of the choice between the own check and the provider's header.

adv_authTrusted.description: Label in front of a text box. $1 is the text box; keep it.

adv_authTrustedPlaceholder.message:
One server per line, for example
mta.yahoo.com
mx.google.com
adv_authTrustedPlaceholder.description: Gray example text in the empty box of trusted servers. Keep the line breaks (\n) and the server names.

adv_authTrustedHint.message: Leave this empty to trust the topmost Authentication-Results header, which your provider adds last. If you enter server names, one per line, the add-on uses the topmost header from one of them. The name is the first word of the header, such as mta.yahoo.com or mx.google.com.
adv_authTrustedHint.description: Explanation of the trusted servers. Keep the text inside … as is.

help_otherFolderTitle.message: A rule misses mail in Sent or another folder that isn't the Inbox
help_otherFolderTitle.description: Help question. Use the names Thunderbird shows for the Sent and Inbox folders in your language.

help_otherFolderCause.message: For IMAP accounts, Thunderbird checks only the Inbox for new mail by default. The add-on can process only messages that Thunderbird has downloaded, so mail that another program sends through your account, or that a server rule files, waits until you open the folder. Run all rules now seems to work because you opened the folder first.
help_otherFolderCause.description: Help answer, part 1. The text inside … is the name of a button (common_runAllRulesNow); use the same translation.

help_otherFolderFix.message: To fix this, right-click the folder and open Properties. On the General tab, turn on When getting new messages for this account, always check this folder.
help_otherFolderFix.description: Help answer, part 2. The text inside each … names a part of Thunderbird; copy the words Thunderbird uses in your language.

help_closedTitle.message: Mail arrived while Thunderbird was closed

help_closedBody.message: Rules run only while Thunderbird is running. After Thunderbird starts, the first scheduled run checks the last 30 days, or the number of days set under Advanced, and processes anything it missed.
help_closedBody.description: Help answer. Advanced is the section heading adv_title; use the same word.

help_otherBody.message: Open Diagnostics and attach the report to a GitHub issue. The report shows what each recent run scanned and matched.
help_otherBody.description: Help answer. Diagnostics is the section heading diag_title. The text inside … becomes the link to the issue tracker; keep the tags.

rule_collapseTitle.description: Tooltip of the arrow button on a rule card.

rule_namePlaceholder.description: Gray text in the empty name box of a rule.

rule_newName.description: Name of a rule the user just added.

rule_enabled.description: Checkbox on a rule card: the rule runs when this is on.

rule_run.description: Button on a rule card that runs only this rule. Keep it short.

rule_runTitle.message: Run only this rule now, on every message in its folders
rule_runTitle.description: Tooltip of the Run button on a rule card.

rule_delete.description: Button that deletes a rule card.

rule_folders.description: Label of the folder list of a rule. The label column is narrow; keep it short.

rule_foldersExpand.description: Small button under the Folders label that opens every account and folder in the list. One short word if you can.

rule_foldersExpandTitle.message: Expand all: show every account and subfolder
rule_foldersExpandTitle.description: Tooltip of the Expand button of the folder list.

rule_foldersCollapse.description: Small button under the Folders label that closes every account in the list. One short word if you can.

rule_foldersCollapseTitle.message: Collapse all: show only the account names
rule_foldersCollapseTitle.description: Tooltip of the Collapse button of the folder list.

rule_folderFilter.description: Gray text and screen reader label of the search box above the folder list.

rule_selectMatching.description: Button that selects every folder the search box shows.

rule_includeSubfolders.message: Include subfolders, and any created later

rule_match.description: Label of the list that chooses between any and all conditions. The label column is narrow; keep it short.

rule_addCondition.description: Button that adds a condition row to a rule.

rule_addAction.description: Button that adds an action row to a rule.

rule_schedule.description: Label of the schedule part of a rule. The label column is narrow; keep it short.

rule_scheduleOn.message: Run this rule on its own schedule
rule_scheduleOn.description: Checkbox that gives a rule its own cron schedule.

rule_cronLabel.description: Screen reader label of the box for the cron expression. Cron is a technical name.

rule_cronHelp.message: How to write a cron expression
rule_cronHelp.description: Link to crontab.guru, an English site that explains cron expressions.

rule_scheduleHint.message: A cron expression has five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, in your computer's local time. With its own schedule, the rule runs only at these times. The timer at the top of the page and new mail no longer start it.

schedule_error.description: Shown under the cron box when the expression is wrong. $1 is the reason (a cron_error message). Change only the final punctuation if your language needs it.

schedule_next.description: Shown under the cron box. $1 is the expression in words (for example "At 21:00 every day"); $2 is the date and time of the next run.

schedule_never.message: $1. This date never comes, so the rule never runs.
schedule_never.description: Shown under the cron box for a date that does not exist, such as February 30. $1 is the expression in words.

cron_fieldMinute.description: Name of the 1st field of a cron expression, used in the cron_error messages.

cron_fieldHour.description: Name of the 2nd field of a cron expression, used in the cron_error messages.

cron_fieldDay.description: Name of the 3rd field of a cron expression, used in the cron_error messages.

cron_fieldMonth.description: Name of the 4th field of a cron expression, used in the cron_error messages.

cron_fieldWeekday.description: Name of the 5th field of a cron expression, used in the cron_error messages.

cron_errorEmpty.description: Error under the empty cron box. No final period: schedule_error adds it.

cron_errorTooLong.description: Error under the cron box. No final period.

cron_errorFieldCount.message: A cron expression has 5 fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. This one has $1
cron_errorFieldCount.description: Error under the cron box. $1 is the number of fields typed. No final period.

cron_errorInvalid.description: Error under the cron box. $1 is the text typed, $2 a field name (cron_field...). No final period. The first letter is made upper case.

cron_errorOutOfRange.description: Error under the cron box. $1 is a field name (cron_field...), $2 and $3 the smallest and largest value, $4 the value typed. The first letter is made upper case. No final period.

cron_errorStep.message: the step "$1" in the $2 must be 1 or more
cron_errorStep.description: Error under the cron box, for a step such as */0. $1 is the step typed, $2 a field name (cron_field...). The first letter is made upper case. No final period.

cron_errorRange.description: Error under the cron box. $1 is the range typed, such as 1-2-3; $2 a field name (cron_field...). No final period.

cron_errorBackwards.description: Error under the cron box, for a range such as 5-1. $1 is the range typed, $2 a field name (cron_field...). The first letter is made upper case. No final period.

cron_range.description: Three or more values in a row in a schedule description, such as "Monday through Friday" or "1 through 5". $1 is the first value and $2 the last.

cron_atTimes.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is a list of clock times, such as "08:30 and 20:30".

cron_everyMinutes_one.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is the number of minutes.

cron_everyMinutes_other.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is the number of minutes.

cron_everyHourOnTheHour.description: A complete schedule description: at minute 0 of every hour.

cron_everyHourAtMinute.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is a minute of the hour, such as 15.

cron_atMinutes_one.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is one minute of the hour.

cron_atMinutes_other.description: Start of a schedule description. $1 is a list of minutes, such as "0 and 30". The plural form follows the number of minutes in the list.

cron_timeAndHours.description: Joins the minutes part and the hours part of a schedule description: "Every 10 minutes, between 09:00 and 17:59". $1 is the minutes part, $2 the hours part.

cron_everyHours_one.description: Hours part of a schedule description. $1 is the number of hours.

cron_everyHours_other.description: Hours part of a schedule description. $1 is the number of hours.

cron_betweenHours.description: Hours part of a schedule description. $1 and $2 are clock times, such as 09:00 and 17:59.

cron_duringHours_one.description: Hours part of a schedule description. $1 is one hour, such as 9.

cron_duringHours_other.description: Hours part of a schedule description. $1 is a list of hours, such as "9 and 12". The plural form follows the number of hours in the list.

cron_everyDay.description: Days part of a schedule description: "At 21:00 every day".

cron_onDaysOfMonth_one.description: Days part of a schedule description. $1 is one day of the month, such as 1.

cron_onDaysOfMonth_other.description: Days part of a schedule description. $1 is a list of days, such as "1 and 15". The plural form follows the number of days in the list.

cron_onWeekdays.description: Days part of a schedule description. $1 is one or more weekday names, such as "Monday through Friday".

cron_inMonths.description: Months part of a schedule description. $1 is one or more month names, such as "January and July".

cron_withDays.description: Joins the time part and the days part of a schedule description: "At 09:00" + "on Monday". Swap $1 and $2 if your language puts the days first.

cron_withMonths.description: Adds the months part to a schedule description: "At 09:00" + "in January". Swap $1 and $2 if your language puts the months first.

folders_account.description: Heading in the folder list for an account that has no name.

folders_includedAsSubfolder.description: Note after a folder name in the folder list: the rule scans this folder because its parent is selected.

folders_selectedInside_one.description: Note after a collapsed folder or account in the folder list. $1 is the number of selected folders it hides.

folders_selectedInside_other.description: Note after a collapsed folder or account in the folder list. $1 is the number of selected folders it hides.

folders_expanded.description: Read by screen readers after the name of a folder whose subfolders are shown.

folders_collapsed.description: Read by screen readers after the name of a folder whose subfolders are hidden.

folders_countSelected_one.description: Count of selected folders, next to the folder search box. $1 is the number.

folders_countSelected_other.description: Count of selected folders, next to the folder search box. $1 is the number.

folders_countSubfolders_one.description: Added to the folder count: folders the rule also scans because a parent is selected. $1 is the number.

folders_countSubfolders_other.description: Added to the folder count: folders the rule also scans because a parent is selected. $1 is the number.

folders_countFiltered_one.description: Added to the folder count: selected folders the search box hides. $1 is the number.

folders_countFiltered_other.description: Added to the folder count: selected folders the search box hides. $1 is the number.

folders_countFolded_one.description: Added to the folder count: selected folders inside a collapsed folder or account. $1 is the number.

folders_countFolded_other.description: Added to the folder count: selected folders inside a collapsed folder or account. $1 is the number.

field_from.description: Condition field: the From header of a message. Lower case in English because it reads as part of a phrase: "from contains …".

field_reply_to.description: Condition field: the Reply-To header. You can keep the header name.

field_list_id.description: Condition field: the List-Id header of a mailing list. You can keep the header name.

field_age.description: Condition field: how many days old the message is.

field_read.description: Condition field: whether the message is read.

field_star.description: Condition field: whether the message has a star.

field_junk.description: Condition field: whether the message is marked as junk.

field_tag.description: Condition field: the Thunderbird tags of the message.

field_priority.description: Condition field: the priority of the message.

field_auth.description: Condition field: the SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks of the sender.

op_contains.description: Condition operator, after a field: "subject contains …".

op_is.description: Condition operator, after a field: "from is …".

op_matchesRegex.description: Condition operator: the field matches a regular expression.

op_domainInList.description: Condition operator: the domain of the address is in a list of domains.

op_inAddressBook.description: Condition operator: the address is in an address book.

op_nameShowsOtherAddress.description: Condition operator: the sender name contains an email address from another domain than the real address.

op_olderThan.description: Condition operator for the age field: "age older than 30 days".

op_newerThan.description: Condition operator for the age field.

op_isOn.description: Condition operator for the read, star, and junk fields. The page replaces it with a state message, such as "is read".

op_isOff.description: Condition operator for the read, star, and junk fields. The page replaces it with a state message, such as "is unread".

op_hasTag.description: Condition operator for the tag field.

op_priorityIs.description: Condition operator for the priority field: "priority is High".

op_authPasses.description: Condition operator for the authentication field: "authentication passes DKIM".

op_greyIsOn.description: Grayed-out operator for a field it does not work with.

op_greyIsOff.message: is unread, not starred, or not junk
op_greyIsOff.description: Grayed-out operator for a field it does not work with.

op_greyPriorityIs.description: Grayed-out operator for a field it does not work with.

op_ageOnly.description: Grayed-out operator. $1 is the operator, such as "older than".

op_ageOnlyReason.message: Works only with the age field.

op_stateOnlyReason.message: Works only with the read, star, and junk fields.

op_tagOnly.description: Grayed-out operator. $1 is the operator, "has tag".

op_tagOnlyReason.message: Works only with the tag field.

op_priorityOnlyReason.message: Works only with the priority field.

op_authOnlyReason.message: Works only with the authentication field.

op_headerOnly.description: Grayed-out operator. $1 is the operator, such as "contains".

op_headerOnlyReason.message: Works only with a header field, such as from or subject.

state_read_isOn.description: Operator text for the read field, and the summary of the condition.

state_read_isOff.description: Operator text for the read field, and the summary of the condition.

state_star_isOn.description: Operator text for the star field, and the summary of the condition.

state_star_isOff.description: Operator text for the star field, and the summary of the condition.

state_junk_isOn.description: Operator text for the junk field, and the summary of the condition.

state_junk_isOff.description: Operator text for the junk field, and the summary of the condition.

priority_highest.description: Message priority. Use the word Thunderbird uses in your language.

priority_high.description: Message priority. Use the word Thunderbird uses in your language.

priority_normal.description: Message priority. Use the word Thunderbird uses in your language.

priority_low.description: Message priority. Use the word Thunderbird uses in your language.

priority_lowest.description: Message priority. Use the word Thunderbird uses in your language.

cond_not.description: Checkbox on a condition row that turns the condition around.

cond_valuePlaceholder.description: Gray text in the empty value box of a condition.

cond_daysUnit.description: Unit after the number box of an age condition.

cond_allowBookAccess.description: Button that asks Thunderbird for permission to read the address books.

cond_allowDnsAccess.description: Button that asks Thunderbird for permission to contact the DNS server.

cond_allAddressBooks.description: Choice in the address book list of a condition.

cond_missingAddressBook.description: Shown for an address book that a rule names but that no longer exists.

cond_domainsPlaceholder.message:
One domain per line, e.g. evil.com
Subdomains are matched automatically.
cond_domainsPlaceholder.description: Gray text in the empty domain list of a condition. Keep the line break (\n) and evil.com.

cond_otherFields.description: Heading in the operator list over the grayed-out operators.

cond_greyFieldList.message: Doesn't work with "domain is in list". Change the operator first.
cond_greyFieldList.description: Tooltip of a grayed-out field. "domain is in list" is the operator op_domainInList; use the same translation.

cond_greyFieldAddress.message: This operator reads addresses, and this field holds none. Change the operator first.

cond_domainListOnly.description: Grayed-out field. $1 is a field set, such as "reply-to or from".

cond_greyDomainSet.message: Works only with the "domain is in list" operator.
cond_greyDomainSet.description: Tooltip of a grayed-out field set. "domain is in list" is the operator op_domainInList; use the same translation.

cond_nameHint.message: Matches when the sender name contains an email address from a different domain than the real address. Example: the name is Lena and the real address is someone@sina.com. Spam does this to look like another sender. Some mailing lists do it too, so try the rule with a move to a folder before you use Trash.
cond_nameHint.description: Explanation under the "name shows a different address" condition. Keep the text inside … as is.

cond_priorityHint.message: To read the priority, the add-on downloads the headers of each message, so this check is slower than the others. A message with no priority counts as Normal.
cond_priorityHint.description: Explanation under a priority condition. Normal is the priority priority_normal.

cond_authHint.message: Checks whether the sender is who the From address claims. To check, the add-on downloads each full message the rule looks at, once, and keeps the result. SPF comes from the Authentication-Results header your mail provider adds. The add-on verifies DKIM itself and works out DMARC from both. If a check can't finish, for example because the DNS server doesn't answer, the condition doesn't match. The add-on tries again for 24 hours. See Advanced for the settings.
cond_authHint.description: Explanation under an authentication condition. Keep Authentication-Results. Advanced is the section heading adv_title.

cond_stateHint.message: A scheduled run checks older mail only in the catch-up scan, by default every 30 minutes (see Advanced). So after you star, tag, or read an older message, the rule can take that long to act on it. Run checks every message at once.
cond_stateHint.description: Explanation under a read, star, junk, or tag condition. Advanced is the section heading adv_title; Run is the button rule_run.

action_then.description: Label in front of an action of a rule. The label column is narrow; keep it short.

action_choose.description: First entry of the action list, before the user picks one.

action_chooseHint.message: Pick what should happen to matching messages.
action_chooseHint.description: Hint under an action row that has no action yet.

action_trash.message: Move to Trash (each message's own account)

action_trashHint.message: Routes each matched message to the Trash of its own account — safe across multi-account rules.
action_trashHint.description: Hint under the Move to Trash action.

action_move.description: Action in the list. The ellipsis means a folder list follows.

action_moveHint.message: Sends every match to the chosen folder — including a folder in a different account (Thunderbird copies to the target account, then deletes the source).
action_moveHint.description: Hint under the Move to folder action.

action_archiveHint.message: Archives each message the way Thunderbird's Archive button does, using its own account's archive settings. An account with archiving turned off keeps its mail in place.

action_copy.description: Action in the list. The ellipsis means a folder list follows.

action_copyHint.message: Leaves the original in place and copies a duplicate into the chosen folder (works across accounts too).
action_copyHint.description: Hint under the Copy to folder action.

action_tag.description: Action in the list. The ellipsis means a tag list follows.

action_tagHint.message: Adds one of your Thunderbird tags. Tags already on the message are kept, so several rules can tag the same mail.

action_markReadHint.message: Marks matches as read without moving them.
action_markReadHint.description: Hint under the Mark as read action.

action_markUnreadHint.message: Marks matches as unread without moving them.
action_markUnreadHint.description: Hint under the Mark as unread action.

action_markFlaggedHint.message: Adds a star to matches without moving them.
action_markFlaggedHint.description: Hint under the Add star action.

action_markUnflaggedHint.message: Removes the star from matches without moving them.
action_markUnflaggedHint.description: Hint under the Remove star action.

action_markJunkHint.message: Marks matches as junk (does not move them — Thunderbird’s junk handling decides the rest).
action_markJunkHint.description: Hint under the Mark as junk action.

action_markNotJunkHint.message: Removes the junk mark from matches without moving them.
action_markNotJunkHint.description: Hint under the Mark as not junk action.

action_deletePermanentlyHint.message: Skips the Trash and deletes matches immediately. This cannot be undone.
action_deletePermanentlyHint.description: Hint under the Delete permanently action, shown in red.

summary_not.description: A turned-around operator in the one-line summary of a folded rule: "from not contains “x”". $1 is the operator.

summary_text.description: A condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the operator, $3 the value typed. Use the quotation marks of your language.

summary_age_one.description: An age condition in the summary of a folded rule: "age older than 1 day". $1 is the field, $2 the operator, $3 the number of days.

summary_age_other.description: An age condition in the summary of a folded rule: "age older than 30 days". $1 is the field, $2 the operator, $3 the number of days.

summary_hasTag.description: A tag condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the tag name.

summary_notHasTag.description: A turned-around tag condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the tag name.

summary_priorityIs.description: A priority condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is a priority, such as High.

summary_priorityIsNot.description: A turned-around priority condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is a priority.

summary_authPasses.description: An authentication condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is SPF, DKIM, or DMARC.

summary_authNotPasses.description: A turned-around authentication condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is SPF, DKIM, or DMARC.

summary_inBook.description: An address book condition in the summary of a folded rule: "from in Personal Address Book". $1 is the field, $2 the address book.

summary_notInBook.description: A turned-around address book condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the address book.

summary_nameShows.description: A condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field.

summary_notNameShows.message: $1 not name shows a different address
summary_notNameShows.description: A turned-around condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field.

summary_inList_one.description: A domain list condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the number of domains.

summary_inList_other.description: A domain list condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the number of domains.

summary_notInList_one.description: A turned-around domain list condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the number of domains.

summary_notInList_other.description: A turned-around domain list condition in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the field, $2 the number of domains.

summary_and.description: Joins the conditions of an all-conditions rule in its summary.

summary_or.description: Joins the conditions of an any-condition rule in its summary.

summary_noConditions.description: Summary of a folded rule with no condition.

summary_noAction.description: Summary of an action row with no action chosen.

summary_tagAction.description: The tag action in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the tag name.

summary_folders_one.description: Number of folders in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the number.

summary_folders_other.description: Number of folders in the summary of a folded rule. $1 is the number.

summary_foldersAndSubfolders_one.description: Number of folders in the summary of a folded rule that includes subfolders. $1 is the number.

summary_foldersAndSubfolders_other.description: Number of folders in the summary of a folded rule that includes subfolders. $1 is the number.

reject_tagActionNoTag.message: rule “$1”: tag action with no tag chosen
reject_tagActionNoTag.description: A correction listed after Saved. $1 is the rule name.

reject_secondTerminal.message: rule “$1”: only one action can move or delete, dropped “$2”
reject_secondTerminal.description: A correction listed after Saved. $1 is the rule name, $2 the action that was dropped.

reject_ageDays.message: age condition needs a whole number of days (got "$1")
reject_ageDays.description: A correction listed after Saved. $1 is the text typed in the days box.

reject_ageDaysEmpty.message: age condition needs a whole number of days (got nothing)
reject_ageDaysEmpty.description: A correction listed after Saved, for an empty days box.

reject_tagConditionNoTag.message: a tag condition has no tag chosen, so it will not match

setting_mustBeOneOf.description: A correction after Saved or Imported. $1 is a setting name, $2 the allowed values (code words, not translated), $3 the value used instead.

import_whereRule.description: Start of an import problem: which rule of the file. $1 is its number.

import_nameFields.message: $1: the name check only applies to $2

import_unknownFolders_one.message: $1: $2 folder not in this profile, removed

import_unknownFolders_other.message: $1: $2 folders not in this profile, removed
